cells.tense: You are handing over what you know in the shape the person in front of you can take it.
cells.ask: Notice what you changed this time to make it land — the wording, the order, the example — and say that change out loud to one person who uses the same material.
cells.core:
You choose what's worth keeping and say it in the shape the people in front of you can take. That's not the same as repeating it. You watch what they can hold and adjust while you're still talking, and what you pass on arrives alive because you changed it on the way.

There are two easy ways to lose that. Say the thing the same way each time and it turns to stone. Hold it so loosely that nobody gets anything to keep. You're doing neither of those right now, which is part of why it works. The cost is that the adjusting has to keep happening. Drop that and you're reciting. So try this — catch what you shifted this time, the wording or the order or the example, and say that shift out loud to someone who works with the same material. Naming it is how you keep it yours.
cells.sheetLine: You adjust what you pass on and it arrives alive.
cells.verb: carrying what has proven worth keeping into the hands of the people in front of you
cells.place: the point where a direction gets chosen and said aloud

cells.tense: You are holding the material so rigidly that it has stopped being usable by the people you are handing it to.
cells.ask: Pick the version people resist most and retire it for one week — not the practice, the wording. Say one piece of it in plainer words than you'd choose.
cells.core:
You've started guarding the handing-over instead of doing it. Anything that comes near the material, you have the right answer ready, and the right answer is the one you were given. Conversation turns into correction. A small deviation and it has to be answered.

What that costs is the thing you're protecting. Transmission needs room for the person receiving it to touch it. When the rule outranks the person, the material is held correctly and stops moving, and you end up alone with something intact that nobody can use. Try this: pick the piece people resist most, and for one week don't touch the practice — touch the wording. Say one part of it in words plainer than your own. The material stays. The seal comes off for a minute.

cells.tense: You are deciding alone on ground you did not learn, and it shows in how little you can hand anyone.
cells.ask: Ask one person older in this work what they tried and dropped. Take only the reason they dropped it, not the method.
cells.core:
You've been picking your direction on ground you didn't stand on. No lineage, no one you learned this from, so the choices get rebuilt from scratch — and you call that independence. It isn't. It means there's nothing under the floor.

Here's how it goes in a room: someone asks why you do it this way and all you have is that you decided to. Then the day's decisions get made by whatever's loudest, and afterward you can't say why. What's short here isn't knowledge. It's connection — some material older than your own thinking to push against.

Go find one person who's done this longer and ask what they tried and then dropped. Don't take the method. Take the reason. Then choose again with something under you, and see what you can hand over once you're standing on something.

cells.tense: You are already the person others copy from, and you have not once said so out loud.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you do that a newer person has already picked up, and tell them once — plainly — that you do it on purpose, and why.
cells.core:
People around you are taking their shape from how you do things. The way you say it, the parts you skip, what you refuse to do when it would be easier — someone newer is copying that and you're acting like it's just how the room is. That teaching is already happening. The part where you own it isn't.

Noticing this isn't vanity. Skipping it is its own decision, made quietly, and it leaves the people copying you with no idea what they're taking or why it's worth taking. None of that requires hiding.

Pick one thing a newer person has already picked up from you. Tell them once that you do it on purpose, and what it's for. One sentence is enough. You don't have to call yourself anything. Just stop leaving that one thing unmanned.
